observation_summary: A StackOverflowError occurs when resolving generic type arguments for interfaces where a generic type has itself as an upper bound, indicating infinite recursion in the type resolution logic.
reasoning_summary: The stack trace shows infinite recursion in 'GenericMetadataSupport.getActualTypeArgumentFor', which is a method responsible for resolving generic types. This is a procedural logic error where the algorithm fails to terminate when encountering self-referential generic bounds, rather than a missing guard (Checking) or a simple value assignment error. It is a local algorithmic failure in the type resolution process.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While a guard could potentially stop the recursion, the root cause is the design of the recursive algorithm itself, which fails to handle self-referential types correctly.
This is a defect in the implementation of an existing method's logic, not a missing capability or design-level omission.
